exposure: early oxytocin perfusion (0-4 hours after amniotomy)
delayed oxytocin perfusion (up to 24 hours after amniotomy, or amniotomy alone if spontaneous labor occurred)
outcome: rate of vaginal delivery (natural or operative)
neonatal complications (severe newborn acidemia, transfer to neonatal intensive care unit)
cohort: Women with a vertex presentation fetus who had an indication for labor induction by amniotomy after 41 weeks of gestation between 2015 and 2022.
finding: Delaying oxytocin administration by 24 hours after amniotomy was associated with a significantly higher rate of vaginal delivery and fewer severe newborn acidemia or NICU transfers.
mod_finding: Delaying oxytocin administration by 24 hours after amniotomy resulted in a significantly higher rate of vaginal delivery.
